title: Osilodrostat in patients with hypertension caused by hypercortisolaemia due to Cushing’s Syndrome
official: A double-blind, randomised, 30-week placebo-controlled phase IV study to assess the efficacy and safety of osilodrostat in patients with hypertension caused by hypercortisolaemia due to Cushing’s Syndrome
summary: Main objective: To evaluate the efficacy of osilodrostat in terms of normalization of urinary-free cortisol (UFC)
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. 1.	Male or female ≥ 18 years of age
2. 2.	Able to provide and have provided signed written informed consent prior to study participation
3. 3.	Diagnosis of endogenous Cushing’s Syndrome
4. 4.	mUFC value from two 24h urinary collections > ULN and ≤ 2x ULN (individual UFCs may fall outside this range)
5. 5.	Participants with uncontrolled hypertension on stable doses of BP lowering medications (for at least 4 weeks); qualifying BP measurements by ABPM taken prior to randomisation defined as: Average of 24h ABPM SBP ≥ 135 mmHg and ≤ 170 mmHg or DBP ≥ 85 mmHg and ≤ 110 mmHg.
6. 6.	Participants under glucocorticoid replacement therapy can be recruited only if this therapy has been already stopped for at least seven days or 5 half-lives prior to screening, whichever was longer
7. 7.	Not taking any drug therapy for CS. The following minimum periods without these medications need to be completed before screening assessments: a.	Steroidogenesis inhibitors (e.g. ketoconazole, metyrapone): 1 week b.	Mifepristone: 3 weeks c.	SC Pasireotide: 1 week d.	Pasireotide LAR: 3 months e.	Cabergoline: 4 weeks
8. 8.	Able to take oral medication and be willing to comply with the requirements of the study
Exclusion criteria:
1. 1.	Previously treated with osilodrostat less than 12 weeks prior to start of screening
2. 10.	Pituitary radiation therapy within 3 years of screening
3. 11.	Ectopic ACTH syndrome or adrenocortical carcinoma with a life expectancy of <3 years or receiving chemotherapy
4. 12.	Having received prior mitotane treatment
5. 13.	Participants who are shift workers or have conditions that can affect the measurement of late-night salivary cortisol (LNSC) or the LDDST
6. 14.	Poorly controlled diabetes mellitus with a baseline HbA1c > 10.5%. Participants receiving glucose lowering medications must be on stable doses for at least 4 weeks prior screening.
7. 15.	Participants who are hypothyroid and not on adequate replacement therapy
8. 16.	History of major surgery/surgical therapy for any cause within 4 weeks before entering the study. Participants should have recovered from the surgery and be in good clinical condition before entering the study
9. 17.	Presence of bradycardia and/or QT-related exclusion criteria.
10. 18.	Total bilirubin > 1.5 x ULN and ALT or AST > 3 x ULN
11. 19.	Participation in any clinical investigation within 4 weeks prior to screening or longer if required by local regulation (Use of an investigational drug within 4 weeks prior to dosing)
12. 2.	Known hypersensitivity to osilodrostat
13. 20.	Occurrence of any significant acute illness within 3 weeks prior to dosing/randomisation
14. 21.	Female participants who are pregnant, intending to become pregnant or breastfeed during the study or lactating, where pregnancy is defined as the state of a female after conception and until the termination of gestation, confirmed by a positive hCG laboratory test
15. 22.	Women of childbearing potential (WOCBP) who are unwilling to use highly effective contraception methods (Section 11.3)
16. 23.	Potentially unreliable or vulnerable participants (e.g. person kept in detention) and those judged by the Investigator to be unsuitable for the study
17. 3.	Presence of any severe and/or uncontrolled medical condition or other conditions that could affect participation in the study
18. 4.	Participants who are scheduled for a surgery to treat CS within 32 weeks of randomisation to the study drug
19. 5.	Presence of a known “long term” history of both hypertension and diabetes (defined as both hypertension and diabetes diagnosed >10 years prior to the initial diagnosis of endogenous CS)
20. 6.	History of cyclic Cushing’s Syndrome with fluctuating clinical manifestations
21. 7.	Participants with pseudo-CS
22. 8.	Participants with compression of the optic chiasm due to a macroadenoma or participants at high risk of compression of the optic chiasm (tumour within 2 mm of optic chiasm)
23. 9.	Participants who have undergone pituitary or adrenal surgery for Cushing’s syndrome within 3 months prior to screening.
